h-bar.name: Reduced Planck Constant
h-bar.description: The fundamental quantum of action, representing the scale at which quantum effects become dominant.

c.name: Speed of Light
c.description: The maximum speed at which all conventional matter and information in the universe can travel.

G.name: Gravitational Constant
G.description: The empirical physical constant involved in the calculation of gravitational effects in Newton's law of universal gravitation and Einstein's theory of general relativity.

k-B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k-B.description: The physical constant relating the average relative kinetic energy of particles in a gas with the thermodynamic temperature of the gas.

epsilon-0.name: Vacuum Permittivity
epsilon-0.description: The capability of the vacuum to permit electric field lines.

mu-0.name: Vacuum Permeability
mu-0.description: The magnetic permeability of classical vacuum.

alpha.name: Fine-structure Constant
alpha.description: The fundamental physical constant characterizing the strength of the electromagnetic interaction between elementary charged particles.

sigma-sb.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Constant
sigma-sb.description: The physical constant relating the total energy radiated per unit surface area of a black body per unit time to the fourth power of the thermodynamic temperature.

wave-function-psi.name: Wave Function
wave-function-psi.description: A complex probability amplitude describing the state of a quantum system.

hamiltonian-operator.name: Hamiltonian Operator
hamiltonian-operator.description: The operator corresponding to the total energy of a quantum system.

metric-tensor-g.name: Metric Tensor
metric-tensor-g.description: A symmetric rank-2 tensor defining distance, geometry, and gravity in spacetime.

energy-momentum-tensor.name: Energy-Momentum Tensor
energy-momentum-tensor.description: A symmetric rank-2 tensor describing the density and flux of energy and momentum in spacetime.

electric-field-E.name: Electric Field
electric-field-E.description: A vector field representing the force exerted per unit charge in space.

magnetic-field-B.name: Magnetic Field
magnetic-field-B.description: A vector field representing magnetic forces exerted on moving electric charges.

mass-m.name: Mass
mass-m.description: A measure of an object's resistance to acceleration and its gravitational attraction.

time-t.name: Time
time-t.description: The progression of events from the past, through the present, into the future.

lagrangian-L.name: Lagrangian Density
lagrangian-L.description: A function representing the difference between kinetic and potential energy density of fields.

nabla-operator.name: Nabla / Gradient Operator
nabla-operator.description: A vector differential operator used to calculate gradients, divergence, and curls of fields.

cosmological-constant-lambda.name: Cosmological Constant
cosmological-constant-lambda.description: The energy density of space, representing dark energy and driving cosmic expansion.

mass-density.name: Mass Density
mass-density.description: The mass per unit volume of a substance, representing the concentration of matter.

speed-of-sound.name: Speed of Sound
speed-of-sound.description: The speed at which acoustic waves propagate through a fluid or elastic medium.

pressure.name: Pressure
pressure.description: The perpendicular force exerted per unit area on the boundary of a system.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: A thermodynamic measure of the average kinetic energy of the constituent particles of a system.

chemical-potential.name: Chemical Potential
chemical-potential.description: The change in free energy when an additional particle is introduced into a thermodynamic system.

magnetic-field.name: Magnetic Field
magnetic-field.description: A vector field representing magnetic forces exerted on moving electric charges.

electric-field.name: Electric Field
electric-field.description: A vector field representing the force exerted per unit charge in space.

velocity.name: Velocity
velocity.description: The rate of change of the position vector of a particle with respect to time.

surface-gravity.name: Surface Gravity
surface-gravity.description: The gravitational acceleration experienced at the surface or event horizon of a massive body.

planck-constant.name: Planck Constant
planck-constant.description: The fundamental constant relating the energy of a photon to its electromagnetic frequency.

gravitational-constant.name: Gravitational Constant
gravitational-constant.description: The empirical physical constant involved in the calculation of gravitational effects in Newtonian and Einsteinian gravity.

current-density.name: Current Density
current-density.description: A vector representing the flow of electric charge per unit area through a cross-section.

elementary-charge.name: Elementary Charge
elementary-charge.description: The electric charge carried by a single proton (or the negative of that carried by an electron).

lagrangian-density.name: Lagrangian Density
lagrangian-density.description: A function representing the difference between kinetic and potential energy density of fields.

wave-vector.name: Wave Vector
wave-vector.description: A vector representing the direction of propagation and phase-frequency spacing of a wave.

quantum-tunneling.name: Quantum Tunneling
quantum-tunneling.description: A quantum mechanical phenomenon where a particle passes through a potential energy barrier higher than its kinetic energy.

coordinate-geometry.name: Coordinate Geometry
coordinate-geometry.description: The spatial coordinate variables used to define positions in a coordinate system.

enthalpy.name: Enthalpy
enthalpy.description: A thermodynamic property equal to the system's internal energy plus the product of its pressure and volume.

internal-energy.name: Internal Energy
internal-energy.description: The total energy contained within a thermodynamic system, including kinetic and potential energies of its particles.

rapidity.name: Rapidity
rapidity.description: A relativistic measure of motion, defined as the hyperbolic angle representing velocity relative to the speed of light.

electric-charge.name: Electric Charge
electric-charge.description: The physical property of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electromagnetic field.

discrete-symmetry.name: Discrete Symmetry
discrete-symmetry.description: A symmetry operation that consists of a finite, non-continuous transformation (e.g. reflection, parity, time reversal).

delta-function.name: Dirac Delta Function
delta-function.description: A generalized function that is zero everywhere except at zero, with an integral of one over the entire real line.

kronecker-delta.name: Kronecker Delta
kronecker-delta.description: A function of two variables, usually integers, which is 1 if they are equal, and 0 otherwise.

levi-civita-tensor.name: Levi-Civita Symbol
levi-civita-tensor.description: An antisymmetric symbol used in tensor calculus to represent permutations and compute vector cross products.

time-derivative.name: Time Derivative
time-derivative.description: The rate of change of a physical variable with respect to time.

acceleration.name: Acceleration
acceleration.description: The rate of change of the velocity vector of a particle with respect to time.

luminosity.name: Luminosity
luminosity.description: The total amount of electromagnetic energy emitted by a celestial object per unit time.

quantum-vacuum.name: Quantum Vacuum
quantum-vacuum.description: The quantum state with the lowest possible energy, containing transient virtual particles.

black-hole-mechanics.name: Black Hole Mechanics
black-hole-mechanics.description: The set of laws relating thermodynamics to the properties of black hole event horizons.

baryons.name: Baryons
baryons.description: Composite subatomic particles made of three quarks, such as protons and neutrons.

entropy.name: Entropy
entropy.description: A thermodynamic measure of molecular disorder, randomness, or information uncertainty.

probability-current.name: Probability Current
probability-current.description: A mathematical flow vector describing the conservation of probability density in quantum mechanics.

transition-temperature.name: Transition Temperature
transition-temperature.description: The critical temperature at which a phase transition occurs in a material (e.g. superconductivity).

b-minus-l-conservation.name: B-L Conservation
b-minus-l-conservation.description: The conservation of the difference between baryon number B and lepton number L in particle physics.

gauge-field-strength.name: Gauge Field Strength
gauge-field-strength.description: The field tensor describing the curvature of a gauge connection in gauge theories.

effective-action.name: Effective Action
effective-action.description: A quantum field theory generating function that accounts for all quantum corrections to the classical action.

faraday-tensor.name: Faraday Tensor
faraday-tensor.description: A mathematical tensor that encapsulates both electric and magnetic fields in relativity.

hopping-parameter.name: Hopping Parameter
hopping-parameter.description: The hopping energy of electrons moving between neighboring atomic sites in crystal lattices.

wave-number.name: Wave Number
wave-number.description: The spatial frequency of a wave, representing the number of cycles per unit distance.

quantum-numbers.name: Quantum Numbers
quantum-numbers.description: Values that describe conserved quantities in quantum systems, such as energy, angular momentum, and spin.
